sql-luatest.note: The NO_ACCESS_PATH transitions in gh_5183_fix_index_field_missing and gh_8418_select_lead_to_assertion preserve the legacy secondary-index route when the primary-only executor cannot represent it. Zero semantic drift is required; this does not close M3.5 or accept M3.7.

sql.note: The reviewed SQL suite exercises the same primary-only no-access-path boundary, residual-filter rejection, and precise reason refinements as SQL-TAP, plus supported planner adoptions. The UNSUPPORTED_EXPRESSION to new_planner transition is exercised by the full-width integer secondary equality/range cases in types.test.lua. The UNSUPPORTED_COLLATION transition is confined to unindexed residual predicates in collation.test.lua (a-vs-b, b-vs-c, and concatenation comparisons); indexed collation access remains guarded on the legacy path. The UNSUPPORTED_FUNCTION transition is deterministic scalar-function projections in collation.test.lua (UPPER/LOWER), gh-4697-scalar-bool-sort-cmp (TYPEOF projection), and types.test.lua (ABS, TYPEOF, QUOTE, LEAST); function-based ORDER BY remains legacy. Exact off/on and repeat semantics are mandatory. iproto.test.lua is excluded because snapshot EXPLAIN changes its asserted EXECUTE counter.

sql-tap.note: Reviewed SQL-TAP transitions include conservative fallback when the primary-only executor would displace a matching secondary-index path, and refinement from unsupported expression to no access path when the primary-only physical route has no candidate. Deterministic scalar residuals (including GREATEST/LEAST in comparisons and IN, TYPEOF comparisons) and LIKE/NOT LIKE are accepted only through the bounded expression contract; indexed LIKE and collated-key access remain on the legacy path. This disposition covers the reviewed unsupported-function-to-new-planner transitions in in1, like3, select1, and tkt-3998683a16; generated-mode off/on and repeat semantic comparisons are exact. Deterministic functions in supported SELECT-list projections now use the new route; function-based ORDER BY remains legacy. Alias-bound predicates in alias.test.lua remain on the legacy path because the test's deterministic UDF has side effects; the reason-only UNSUPPORTED_FUNCTION to UNSUPPORTED_FILTER refinement for q06-q10 preserves their exact results. ORDER BY cases that cannot form the new physical route remain on current_where_c. Focused tests pin the residual grammar and index guard.
